> This article documents two errors found after publication of Mana et al.
([2026](https://doi.org/10.1177/1877718X261450361)) and lists every published
result affected by their correction. Both errors were reported by
[elliottower](https://github.com/elliottower) in issues
[#20](https://github.com/josefmana/demcrit/issues/20) and
[#21](https://github.com/josefmana/demcrit/issues/21). The corrections were made
by Jožka Mana and have not been reviewed by the other authors or by the journal.
**None of the conclusions of the article change.**

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(demcrit)

data("rates")
data("concords")
data("rates_published")
data("concords_published")

algos <- list_algorithms(rates)
algos_pub <- list_algorithms(rates_published)

kap <- summarise_kappa(algos, concords)$sums
kap_pub <- summarise_kappa(algos_pub, concords_published)$sums

msd <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f%% (SD = %.2f)", mean(x), sd(x))
faq_tot <- function(d) d$perc[d$IADL == "FAQ > 7"]

smoca_sens <- function(d) {
  subset(d, predictor == "sMoCA (1)" & reference == "Lvl.II (1)")$Sensitivity |>
    sprintf(fmt = "%.2f")
}

n_pairs <- range(concords_published$N, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## What was wrong

1. **MoCA threshold.** Table 1 of the article states that MoCA-based algorithms
   define global cognitive deficit as MoCA < 27. The code applied MoCA < 26, the
   same value as was stated in the Appendix to the article. The code now applies
   MoCA < 27, as stated in the article.

2. **Missing data in the concordance analysis.** The Methods state that analyses
   were done on complete cases (N = 190). The concordance statistics (Cohen's κ,
   accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) were instead computed on all cases
   available for each pair of algorithms (N = `r n_pairs[1]` to `r n_pairs[2]`).
   They are now computed on the 190 complete cases, as stated in the article.

The values printed in the article are distributed with the package as
`rates_published` and `concords_published`. Version 1.2.0 of the package
reproduces the article as printed:

```{r}
#| label: install-published
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

devtools::install_github("josefmana/demcrit@v1.2.0")
```

## Changed statements

```{r}
#| label: tbl-statements

data.frame(
  Location = c(
    "Abstract; Results (Concordance between algorithms)",
    "Abstract; Results (Concordance between algorithms)",
    "Results (Dementia rate estimates)",
    "Results (Dementia rate estimates)",
    "Results (Descriptive analysis)"
  ),
  Quantity = c(
    "Cohen's κ, same IADL definition (FAQ total)",
    "Cohen's κ, IADL definitions differ",
    "Mean PDD rate, all algorithms",
    "Mean PDD rate, FAQ total algorithms",
    "sMoCA sensitivity for Level II (FAQ total)"
  ),
  Published = c(
    kap_pub["faq_tot"], kap_pub["iadl"],
    msd(rates_published$perc), msd(faq_tot(rates_published)),
    smoca_sens(concords_published)
  ),
  Corrected = c(
    kap["faq_tot"], kap["iadl"],
    msd(rates$perc), msd(faq_tot(rates)),
    smoca_sens(concords)
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

In addition, the following tables and figures change accordingly: Table A3
(rates per algorithm), Tables A4 and A5 (best and worst approximations of Level
II), Figure 1 (dot sizes and bold edges), Figure 2 and Figures A7 to A9
(concordance matrices), and Figures A4 to A6 (rates and their demographic
predictors).

## What does not change

- The range and median of PDD rate estimates (2.11% to 16.84%, Md = 4.21%), and
  all algorithms using FAQ item 9 to define IADL deficit.
- Cohen's κ among algorithms using FAQ item 9 (`r kap["faq_9"]`).
- All MMSE-based, sMoCA-based and Level II algorithms.
- The exploratory variable selection, the screening model (MoCA Five words and
  MMSE Sevens), Table 3 and Figure 3, which do not depend on the MoCA total
  score.
- The verbal conclusions: top-ranked Level I algorithms are MoCA-based and
  mostly use Clock drawing and Animal naming; sMoCA achieves the highest
  balanced accuracy for Level II (FAQ total) classification.

## Changed PDD rates

The corrected threshold changes the classification of
`r sum(rates$perc != rates_published$perc[match(rates$type, rates_published$type)])`
of 68 algorithms, all MoCA-based with IADL deficit defined by FAQ total score.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rates

cmp <- merge(
  rates_published[, c("type", "Executive", "Memory", "Language", "Rate")],
  rates[, c("type", "Rate", "perc")],
  by = "type",
  suffixes = c(" (published)", " (corrected)")
)
cmp <- cmp[cmp$`Rate (published)` != cmp$`Rate (corrected)`, ]
cmp <- cmp[order(-cmp$perc), setdiff(names(cmp), "perc")]
names(cmp)[1] <- "Algorithm"
knitr::kable(cmp, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Corrected Tables A4 and A5

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Table A4 (accuracy), corrected

```{r}
#| label: tbl-a4

table_levelII_approximations(concords, algos, "Accuracy_raw")$gtable
```

### Table A4, published

```{r}
#| label: tbl-a4-pub

table_levelII_approximations(concords_published, algos_pub, "Accuracy_raw")$gtable
```

### Table A5 (balanced accuracy), corrected

```{r}
#| label: tbl-a5

table_levelII_approximations(concords, algos, "Balanced Accuracy")$gtable
```

### Table A5, published

```{r}
#| label: tbl-a5-pub

table_levelII_approximations(concords_published, algos_pub, "Balanced Accuracy")$gtable
```

:::

## Corrected manuscript

A corrected author version of the manuscript, generated from
`_manuscript/manuscript.qmd` in this repository, is attached to the
[v2.0.0 release](https://github.com/josefmana/demcrit/releases/tag/v2.0.0).
